topic: Acceptability and feasibility of public square dancing for community senior citizens with mild cognitive impairment and depressive symptoms: A pilot study

sources.title: Acceptability and feasibility of public square dancing for community senior citizens with mild cognitive impairment and depressive symptoms: A pilot study
sources.authors: Yao X, Zhao Y, Yin M, Li Z.

findings.finding: Senior citizens successfully maintained participation in public square dancing throughout the intervention and follow-up periods.
findings.quote: During the intervention, 90.6% of senior citizens met the requirement for defined hours. All senior citizens continued to dance at the three-month follow-up, and 32.3% met the requirement for defined hours.

findings.finding: Participation in public square dancing led to significantly higher psychological well-being scores among the participants.

principle: Public square dancing is an acceptable and feasible intervention that can improve psychological well-being for senior citizens with mild cognitive impairment and depressive symptoms.
for_the_teacher: Design public square dancing sessions that are structured to be accessible and feasible for older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study was conducted specifically with community-dwelling senior citizens with mild cognitive impairment and depressive symptoms.
